prs.title: Fix: form reset in select
prs.author: Bhavani2016
prs.body:
Closes #10642

### Summary
A Select with more than 300 items should restore its default selection when the form resets, even without a name.

Previously, no hidden input was rendered in this case, so the reset listener could not attach to the form. This change renders the input regardless of name, allowing the existing reset logic to work.

Added tests for 300 and 301 items, with and without a name, including form submission checks and React Aria Components interaction tests.

prs.title: fix: form reset with there are multiple selections in CheckboxGroup
prs.author: Bhavani2016
prs.body:
Closes #10643

When a form resets a CheckboxGroup with multiple selected values, one checkbox can remain selected. The goal is for every checkbox to return to the group's default selection.

removeValue previously calculated each removal from the values captured by the render. When multiple removals happen in the same update, a later removal can restore a value removed earlier. This change uses a functional state update so each removal sees the latest values.

The change adds a React Aria Components regression test for both CheckboxField and Checkbox, plus a React Stately test for multiple removals in one update.

prs.title: fix(react-aria): only announce combobox section changes to VoiceOver
prs.author: gonzoblasco
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #10220: ComboBox only announced the item name with VoiceOver, losing the richer native announcement (selected state, menu item role, item count).

## Root cause

On Apple devices, `useComboBox` announces every focused-item change through a live region. Current VoiceOver versions announce per-item details (selected state, role, item count) natively while arrowing within a section, so that live-region announcement interrupts and replaces the richer native speech with just the item name.

## Change

Gate the manual announcement so it only fires when navigating into a new section, where VoiceOver is silent and the section title + option count are not announced natively. Arrowing within the same section no longer triggers a manual announcement, letting VoiceOver handle it.

This keeps the inter-section navigation announcements (section title + option count) that were the reason the effect existed, while no longer stomping on VoiceOver's native per-item announcements.

## Tests

- Updated the combobox announcement tests to assert that per-item navigation no longer triggers a manual announcement, while section-entry announcements are preserved.
- 218 tests pass in `packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js`.
- 41 tests pass in `packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js`.

prs.title: fix(Toolbar): scroll keyboard-focused items fully into view
prs.author: devteamaegis
prs.body:
Closes #5885

**Intent:** when you arrow-key through a toolbar that is clipped by an overflow container, the newly focused item should end up fully visible, not left partly cut off.

**Root cause:** `useToolbar` moves focus with `focusManager.focusNext()` / `focusPrevious()`, which just call `element.focus()`. Browsers don't scroll on `focus()` when the element is already partly visible, so an item that is clipped by a few pixels stays clipped after it gets focus.

**Fix:** after an arrow key moves focus, call `scrollIntoViewport(nextFocused, {containingElement: ref.current})` on the element the focus manager returned. That's the same helper `useSelectableCollection` uses for keyboard navigation (it also passes the collection ref as `containingElement`). It only runs for arrow-key navigation, not Tab/Shift+Tab or pointer focus, so clicking an item doesn't scroll anything.

A previous attempt (#7538) did the scrolling in `onFocus`, gated on `getInteractionModality()`. That needed a new `@react-aria/interactions` dependency, and the author closed it without review. Doing it in the keydown handler avoids the modality check, because it only runs when the toolbar itself moved focus.

prs.title: fix: don't inherit parent Form props in a nested Form
prs.author: UditDewan
prs.body:
Closes #10740

A RAC `Form` both provides and consumes `FormContext` via `useContextProps`, so a `Form` rendered inside another `Form` in the React tree (e.g. an independent form in a `Modal`) merged in the outer form's props: chained `onSubmit`, duplicated `id`/`className`, and inherited `validationErrors`.

**Intent:** a nested `Form` should be independent, while a `FormContext` provided by the user (not by a `Form`) should keep working as it does today.

**Implementation:** following the suggestion in the issue, `Form` now adds a private symbol to the `FormContext` value it provides. When a `Form` sees that marker on the incoming context, it skips merging it (passing `slot: null` to `useContextProps`, the existing "don't use context" escape hatch). Fields are unaffected: they only read `validationBehavior` from `FormContext`, and still get it from their nearest `Form`.

prs.title: fix: runAfterTransition retains elements when multiple transitions are cancelled
prs.author: ali-idrizi
prs.body:
Closes #7326

We noticed a memory leak issue in an app, and tracked it down to the same issue as explained in #7326.

`runAfterTransition` registers its `transitioncancel` listener with `{once: true}`. Browsers dispatch one `transitioncancel` per property (verified in Chrome 148 and Firefox 150). So when an element with two or more running transitions has them cancelled, only the first property is removed, and the listener detached. The element then stays in `transitionsByElement` indefinitely.

This has two effects:

- **Removed from the DOM mid-transition**: the element and its detached subtree are retained until something calls `runAfterTransition` again and `cleanupDetachedElements()`
- **Still connected** (e.g. `display: none`): `cleanupDetachedElements()` never removes it, so the map never empties. Every later `runAfterTransition` callback on the page never fires

The fix removes `once`. `onTransitionEnd` already removes the listener once the element has no transitioning properties left.

prs.title: fix: avoid an extra render on mount in useDescription
prs.author: tabedzki
prs.body:
:robot: _AI text below_ :robot:

Related: #2504, #9738

## Summary

**Intent:** components that use `useDescription` (every draggable via `useDrag`, plus tags, table column resizing and others) shouldn't need a second render on mount just to pick up the id of a description node that already exists.

**What was happening:** `useDescription` stores the id in state that always starts as `undefined`, then sets it in a layout effect, including when the shared node for that description is already there. Every component therefore rendered twice on mount, and the second render was a synchronous update from the layout phase. In a virtualized list with draggable rows, each row scrolled into view scheduled one of these. In Actual Budget this kept React from ever finishing a commit with no pending work while the user scrolled quickly, and React 19 threw "Maximum update depth exceeded" (actualbudget/actual#9170).

**Change:** initialize the state lazily from the existing node. When the node exists, the layout effect sets the same id the state already holds, so React skips the update. Only the component that creates the node still re-renders once. Ref counting, node cleanup and description changes behave as before. This is smaller in scope than the `aria-description` direction discussed in #9738, and doesn't get in its way.

**Tests:** added a test in `dnd.test.js` showing that draggables mounting after the description exists commit once, with no extra update, and point at the shared node,
